prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the outdoor scene's 3D layout, showing a receding brick wall on the left (1–2 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach at the near edge), a sloped lawn underneath, a foreground person at the bottom (0.5–1.2 m away, within arm's reach), a row of parked cars on the right (10–25 m away, about 1 m apart from each other), and background trees above and behind (15–30 m away). Across the five frames, the foreground person shifts from the bottom-left with a raised arm in frame 1 to a lower head-and-shoulders profile in frame 2, drops mostly out of view below the bottom-center edge in frames 3–4 as the camera wearer moves forward and levels the camera roll near the left wall, and rises back into view at the bottom-center in frame 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map more clearly displays the continuous distance gradient along the brick wall and ground plane, as well as the depth separation of the tree trunk (~15 m ahead) and a tiny distant figure beside it (~18 m ahead) in frames 3–4. However, it provides only flat silhouettes that obscure whether the foreground person faces toward or away from the camera wearer, merges the adjacent parked cars into indistinct steps, and shifts per-frame brightness normalization so the foreground head looks darker (farther) in frames 3–5 despite remaining within 1 m.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the close foreground `person` at the bottom-left to bottom-center (0.5–1.2 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach) and the diagonal line of `car` instances on the right (10–25 m away, positioned side-by-side and partially occluding one another from right to left), while leaving the left wall, lawn, and trees unmasked. Across the five frames, the `person` mask shows the raised left arm in frame 1, the head and shoulders in frame 2, severe bottom-edge occlusion where only the top of the head remains visible in frames 3–4, and the head rising again in frame 5, while the car masks shift toward the lower right as the camera rotates upright. Unlike the depth map or small RGB frames, instance segmentation clearly delineates individual overlapping cars in the mid-ground parking row and highlights a tiny distant feature (`bench`) roughly 18 m ahead near the tree in frame 4. However, the map is unreliable for full spatial layout because it omits the nearby brick wall within arm's reach on the left, cannot indicate which way the blurred person faces or looks, and inconsistently fragments distant cars into overlapping masks while mislabelling the distant dog/object in frame 4 as a `bench`.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank across frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, showing only a single compact yellow body-keypoint cluster in frame 2 located at the bottom-left, roughly 1 m in front of and below the camera wearer (within arm's reach). In frame 2, the arrangement of head and shoulder keypoints indicates the foreground person is below eye level with their torso angled mostly toward the camera wearer and slightly to the right, while their lower body is cut off below the bottom frame boundary. Where the RGB image heavily blurs the person's head, this skeleton cluster provides explicit landmark positions for the head and shoulders in frame 2. However, the map is largely unreliable because it misses the foreground person in four of the five frames—including the raised arm and hand in frame 1 (producing no magenta hand skeletons anywhere) and the partially occluded head in frames 3–5—and provides no information about the distant person near the trees (~18 m away) or the surrounding building, ground, and cars.
